source.title: Noise Stability Optimization for Finding Flat Minima: A Hessian-based Regularization Approach
source.authors: Hongyang R. Zhang; Dong-Yue Li; Hao-Tian Ju

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies Hessian regularization and generalization. Its experiments do not test the training-error claims in the listed versions; cited background and setup statements do not count as results for them.
record.gate_note: The ResNet-34 CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 results report test accuracy and Hessian trace, not training classification error. The paper's near-zero training-loss statement for MLP, BERT, and GCN appears as setup for a Hessian-approximation measurement, not as a reported result. The matrix-sensing simulation explicitly reports near-zero training MSE, which is recorded under fits_no_version because it is a regression result, not benchmark classification error.
record.test_reason: The study measures Hessian regularization and generalization, without testing any listed version. CIFAR results report test accuracy and Hessian statistics. Table 2 reports training accuracy for pretrained ResNet-34 fine-tuning on other datasets, outside V1's random-initialization CIFAR setting. Matrix-sensing convergence and divergence do not establish V5's stability-threshold dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that two-point noise injection regularizes the Hessian and improves generalization across their fine-tuning, pretraining and instruction-tuning experiments. Their generalization bound describes measured differences after training but does not independently explain why NSO outperforms naive weight-noise injection.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates Hessian regularization by weight-noise injection and does not apply the methods or measurements in the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: The matrix-sensing simulation reports near-zero training MSE for GD, WP-GD and NSO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested gradient-based methods can interpolate the over-parameterized matrix-sensing training data.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports 100% training accuracy for standard SGD fine-tuning on all three downstream datasets, with lower accuracy under some noise-injection conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained ResNet-34 can fit these downstream classification datasets completely; weight-noise regularization can reduce training accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Matrix-sensing learning rates of 0.005 and 0.01 produce exploding loss, without a measured stability threshold or recovery analysis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large fixed learning rates can cause divergence in the tested matrix-sensing problem.

record.problems: For the matrix-sensing training-MSE result, the text gives no numeric values or uncertainty; results are presented in Figure 6. The paper reports five-run uncertainty for other experiments, but those metrics do not measure the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error for randomly initialized convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and dependence on size, stopping or regularization.
Spurious-minimum frequency and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.
Effects of activation-matched initialization and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights on training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery above an initial stability threshold, accompanying curvature dynamics, sustained edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence relative to measured thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free training.

record.verdict_notes: The appendix's near-zero training-loss statement concerns MLP, BERT and GCN models used for Hessian-approximation measurements; it does not supply V1's specified architecture, dataset and training-error evidence. Related-work discussion of edge-of-stability results supplies no new test of V5.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima frequency, and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects in plain versus residual networks and the effects of special initialization or normalization removal on training error.
Activation-matched initialization, depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and training speed or trainable depth.
Training dynamics above or near a stability threshold, including curvature and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free residual training.

rows.subject: matrix sensing problem; GD, WP-GD, and NSO (reported together)
rows.operation_detail: Full-gradient updates on the matrix-sensing objective from Gaussian initialization; the text reports the three algorithms together.

conditions.value: 0.0025 for the top panel; 0.0001 for the bottom panel

rows.value: All three algorithms can reduce the training MSE to near zero.
rows.note: The text gives an aggregate qualitative result for GD, WP-GD, and NSO; the plotted curves are not separately transcribed. This is matrix-sensing regression, not classification on CIFAR benchmarks.
rows.check: Near-zero matrix-sensing training MSE is reported, but cannot determine any listed version's effect. Split the conditions: Figure 6a includes GD, WP-GD and NSO; Figure 6d includes only WP-GD and NSO. The caption gives the bottom-panel learning rate as 0.0001, whereas the simulation prose says 0.001.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
